塞特琴屬波斯傳統音樂中的長頸魯特琴，起源時間有九世紀推測，另有十五世紀或更早的保: The setar is a long-necked lute of Persian traditional music; its origin has been conjectured to the ninth century, with a conservative estimate of the fifteenth century or earlier. It originally had three strings, and a fourth was added around the nineteenth century, traditionally credited to the Sufi musician Moshtaq Ali Shah; the four strings still fall into three groups. In recent centuries its tuning and playing style have been closer to the tar. Instruments of the same name are found in Tajikistan, Balochistan, Pakistan, Xinjiang and India, though these do not necessarily represent direct descent.

The setar is a long-necked plucked instrument of Persian/Iranian traditional music, a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.321, a member of the tanbur family. Its pear-shaped soundbox joins a slender neck, on which movable frets are wound from gut or silk; today it usually has four strings, though its name comes from "three strings". The player sits with the body set diagonally on the right thigh, plucks with a swinging motion of the right index finger and stops the strings with the left to choose notes, and may play solo or accompany singing.
塞特琴琴身多以桑木或胡桃木製成，可整塊挖製或以木片黏合；面板為薄木片，琴橋為木製: The setar's body is mostly of mulberry or walnut, either carved from one piece or built from glued boards; the soundboard is a thin plate of wood, the bridge is wooden, and the neck may be decorated with camel bone. The movable frets on the neck are wound from animal gut or silk, and nylon is also seen. Of the four strings, the bass string and the yellow string are bronze or phosphor bronze, and the drone string and the silver string are steel. The source gives no materials for the other parts.
塞特琴用於波斯傳統音樂，可獨奏，也可為人聲伴奏。它屬於長頸魯特琴家族，以右手食指: The setar is used in Persian traditional music, both solo and to accompany singing. It belongs to the long-necked lute family, is plucked with the index finger of the right hand, and its tuning and playing style are close to the tar. The source does not mention specific composers or pieces, so no works are listed; in listening one can attend to its solo or accompanying sound.
塞特琴音色溫潤而富有詩意，兼具明亮與幽深的雙重特質。其高音區清澈透亮，具有絲綢般: The setar's timbre is warm and poetic, combining brightness with depth. Its high register is clear and translucent, with a silk-like softness; its low register is mellow and warm, giving a mood of meditation. Its range is wide, more than two and a half octaves, and it can express delicate intervallic changes. Because it follows the lute design, its resonator is compact and produces a warm, penetrating sound. Beside the bright, clean guitar the setar's timbre is softer and more inward; beside the heavy, dull oud it is clearer and more agile. Plucking with the index finger gives the instrument a distinctive control, letting it express the complex, subtle microtones of Persian classical music and creating a meditative Eastern atmosphere.
演奏塞特琴時，演奏者坐姿，琴身斜置於右大腿，約呈四十五度角。初學先依調式或歌者音: In playing the setar the player sits with the body set diagonally on the right thigh, at about forty-five degrees. A beginner first tunes the strings to the mode or the singer's range, and can move the frets wound on the neck to adjust pitch and microtones. Sound is made by a swinging pluck of the right index finger while fingers of the left hand stop the strings on the frets; usually the lowest melody string is practised first, and only harder passages add the other fingers or the thumb on the bass string.
